title: Synthetic scheduler: validate before allocating
query: How should a scheduler validate completed jobs and integer fields?
content: Validate every job before scheduling, including already completed jobs. Reject boolean costs, priorities and budgets despite Python bool inheriting int. Required fields cannot default silently. Canonical identifiers are nonempty strings equal to their stripped form; case matters. All invalid inputs raise ValueError.

title: Synthetic scheduler: cycles and completed dependencies
query: Which dependency cycles must the scheduler reject?
content: Reject unknown dependencies and every self dependency, including on completed jobs. Check cycles among noncompleted jobs independently of affordability. An already completed identifier satisfies its outgoing dependents and must not be included as an unresolved cycle vertex. External completed IDs and duplicate dependency entries are allowed.

title: Synthetic scheduler: recompute affordable eligibility
query: How should scheduler priorities interact with budgets and dependencies?
content: After each single selection, recompute all eligible affordable jobs. Select the highest priority and then the lexicographically smallest ID. An unaffordable high-priority job cannot stop an affordable lower-priority one. Newly satisfied dependent jobs may outrank jobs that were already ready.

title: Synthetic scheduler: preserve caller-owned inputs
query: What mutation rules apply to job and budget allocation?
content: Jobs, their nested dependency lists, budgets and completed input must be unchanged on success and failure. Work on separate state. Return all provider balances, including unused providers. Already completed jobs consume no budget and appear in neither scheduled nor blocked.

title: Synthetic scheduler: classify final blocked reasons
query: When should unscheduled jobs be classified as budget or dependency blocked?
content: Compute reasons after scheduling stops, against the final completed set. A remaining job is budget blocked only when every dependency is satisfied; otherwise it is dependency blocked. Emit blocked IDs in lexicographic order. The scheduling result must not depend on input job order.

title: Synthetic scheduler: valid boundary cases
query: Which zero-cost and empty-input scheduling cases are valid?
content: Zero-cost jobs and negative integer priorities are valid. Duplicate completed IDs and duplicate dependency entries are allowed. Empty jobs and empty budgets are valid when no jobs require a provider. Completed identifiers may refer to jobs outside the supplied list. Validate integer types exactly and keep missing fields distinct from valid zero values.
